$meta.procedure: Figma variables -> design/figma-variables/*.json (DTCG export, committed, see design/figma-variables/README.md for provenance/refresh) -> this file is a curated mirror (see CLAUDE.md / ADR-0010; naming rule + alias tier added by #203). Then run `pnpm sync:tokens` to regenerate app/theme.css. Never edit app/theme.css by hand. `pnpm check:tokens-drift` verifies this file still matches the export (see design/tokens.json's own semantic.$comment, #203 paragraph, for the $pendingFigmaValue escape hatch).

duration.$comment: Ticket #86: Figma carries no prototype reactions/transitionDuration on the Sidebar component set (or anywhere else in this file) — there is no Figma value to resolve here, only a codebase-picked default. See design/tokens.json's semantic.$comment and docs/open-questions.md#sidebar-motion-timing-unsourced.

easing.$comment: Ticket #86: same caveat as duration above — no Figma source. 'out' deliberately matches the standard ease-out cubic-bezier CSS already ships as its own default `ease-out` utility (see node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css) so the curve itself is not a new invention, only its promotion to a named project token is.

semantic.$comment: A plain string ref is a light-only token (no dark variant yet). An object { light, dark } carries a dark-mode override. `pnpm sync:tokens` emits the dark refs into a `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }` block in app/theme.css — that attribute is what Ladle's Light/Dark toggle sets on <html> (see @ladle/react's init-side-effects.ts); it's also the hook the real app would use once it grows its own theme switch (not built yet, out of scope for #42). Dark values below are this round's addition (2026-07-20, ticket #42), scoped to the primitives Atom/Button actually uses — no Figma dark-mode frames exist to fetch, so these are derived by staying inside Tailwind's stock stone/red scale rather than inventing one-off hex. Not every token has a dark counterpart yet; that's a flagged gap for a future token-sync pass, not an oversight. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20, supersedes #52's state tier): Figma added a FOURTH state to Button/Default and redistributed the values. What #52 recorded as Hover is now Active (pressed); Hover took a milder new value; Selected no longer changes the background at all — it only darkens the text to `text`. The scale is therefore `role` / `role-hover` / `role-active`, and the `*-selected` colour tokens #52 added (surface-selected, surface-raised-selected, border-selected, priority-urgent-bg-selected) were REMOVED rather than left as dead names — Selected needs no background token. `surface-hover` changed from stone-300 (which had no consumer) to stone-50 and now backs Button/White's Hover; `surface-active` (stone-100) shares its primitive with `surface-muted` but is kept as a separate name because it is a distinct role — a state colour, not a static surface. TICKET #58 (2026-07-20): re-fetched Atom/Input-field (node 3705:4402) expecting it to have been re-bound onto Button's shared border/border-hover/border-active scale now that Figma redistributed a fourth state (Selected) onto it. It has NOT: Default matches Button's Default (stone-300, so it keeps reading the shared `border` token, no component-scoped token needed there), but Hover (stone-500) and the new Active (a value with no prior primitive, added this ticket as `stone-600`) are genuinely different pixels from Button/Outline's Hover (stone-400) and Active (stone-700) — confirmed by fetching both nodes side by side, not assumed. The good news: the #56-era bug (Hover darker than Active, backwards from Button) is gone — Hover (stone-500) is now correctly lighter than Active (stone-600), same direction as Button. So this is no longer a stale/unbound node; it is a deliberately distinct border ramp, kept under its own tokens rather than forced onto Button's. `border-input-focus` is renamed `border-input-active` (it reads Figma's actual `Active` state; the old name described this atom's `:focus-within` *interpretation* of that state, which still holds — see design/figma-map.json). `border-input-hover` keeps its stone-500 value unchanged. Now that this node carries the SAME four state names as Atom/Button, its CSS hooks follow the same semantics Button established in #56, so all four states are modelled: Hover -> `hover:`, Active -> `active:` (Figma's Active means 'being pressed', which is what CSS :active means), Selected -> `:focus-within`. Selected is the state whose sample shows a typed value (text stone-950) rather than the placeholder, i.e. the field has been engaged - which is exactly what :focus-within expresses, and it is a better fit than the pre-#58 reading that put :focus-within on Active. That mapping is still this atom's interpretation (Figma labels states, not CSS hooks) and stays flagged in design/figma-map.json for confirmation. `border-input-selected` (stone-400) backs it. Dark values remain this codebase's own pick (no Figma dark frames exist); the destructive hover/active pair still both resolve to red-950 in dark mode, i.e. those states are invisible there — a known, flagged gap, not an oversight. Figma MCP still returns resolved hex only, never variable names, so every semantic name here is derived from values, not read from Figma. TICKET #68 (2026-07-20): re-fetched Atom/Button (3623:4346) and Atom/Input-field (3705:4402) again, per the ticket's premise that the user re-authored Button/Outline's borders since #58. Confirmed, pixel-for-pixel, not assumed: three of the four states now match between the two components. `border-hover` moves stone-400 -> stone-500 (Button/Outline's Hover stroke, fill_974f0cf9/#79716B in the fetched node) — this is exactly Input-field's existing `border-input-hover` value, so that token is deleted and InputField.tsx now reads the shared `border-hover`; its dark pairing (stone-400) is carried over unchanged from the deleted token, not re-derived. `border-active` moves stone-700 -> stone-800 (Button/Outline's Active stroke, #292524 in the fetched node) — Button-only; Input-field's Active (stone-600) still does not match this, so `border-input-active` is kept as the one remaining, deliberately-flagged divergence (see docs/design-tokens.md open question 1). A new `border-selected` token (stone-400, fill_5bc671a0/#A6A09B in Button's fetched node) is added: Outline's Selected state gained a border change for the first time since #56 (previously 'border unchanged, text -> text'), and this same stone-400 value is exactly Input-field's existing `border-input-selected`, so that token is deleted too and InputField.tsx now reads the shared `border-selected` on its `:focus-within` hook. `border-selected`'s dark value (stone-500) is likewise carried over unchanged from the deleted `border-input-selected` token. Note for anyone reading #56's history above: `border-selected` was removed in #56 because Selected stopped carrying any colour at all; it is legitimately back now that Figma's Outline/Selected state has a border again — this is not a mistake or a regression of #56's decision, it is a new, independently-confirmed Figma fact. `border-active`'s new dark value (stone-200, was stone-300) is this codebase's own pick, not Figma-sourced (no dark frames exist): the light value got one shade darker (700->800) so the dark counterpart was moved one shade lighter (300->200) to preserve the same relative contrast direction the token already had, consistent with how `border`/`border-hover` pair their light/dark shades on either side of the stone scale's midpoint elsewhere in this file. Button.tsx's Outline variant gains `aria-pressed:border-border-selected` for the first time, which puts Selected in direct competition with Hover/Active on `border-color` — previously impossible, since Selected touched only `text`. Verified against the compiled `pnpm ladle:build` stylesheet (documented in the PR) that hover/active still visually override Selected's border on a selected button, using compound `aria-pressed:hover:`/`aria-pressed:active:` variants (higher specificity than the plain `aria-pressed:` rule) rather than relying on Tailwind's variant emission order, which is not something this codebase controls or should assume. TICKET #203 (2026-08-11): Figma MCP's get_variable_defs turned out to return real variable names after all (verified on 3623:4346 and 3705:4402), which invalidated this file's founding assumption that every name here was hex-derived guesswork. design/figma-variables/*.json is now the committed DTCG export of the actual Figma variable collections (Primitives/Tailwind, Semantics/Style Light+Dark, Semantics/Responsive Mobile+Desktop), and this PR renames every semantic colour token onto its canonical Figma variable path: `color/` stripped, `Stroke` -> `stroke`, trailing `/default` dropped, and the `text/base/*` group drops the `base` segment (a Figma folder, not a role) — e.g. `color/surface/primary/default` -> `surface-primary`, `color/text/base/primary` -> `text-primary`. This is a RENAME ONLY: every value below is still the pre-#203 value, byte-identical, even on the 13 tokens whose light or dark value the Figma export actually disagrees with (marked `$pendingFigmaValue`, light/dark + `ticket: 204` — resolving those is #204's job, and `pnpm check:tokens-drift` skips exactly what that field marks). Two named exceptions: `surface-hover` (stone-50) has no Figma counterpart at all — kept under its existing name with `figma: null` and a reason (see its own entry); and `accent` (`#8A38F5`, `primitive.color.purple-figma`) is deleted outright — not in Figma, and its last non-obvious consumer (Icon.stories.tsx's Sizes demo) is moved onto `text-highlight-blue` (Architecture.md §3.2 and docs/guides/ui-components.md updated). The eight product aliases (`priority-urgent(-bg)`, `priority-medium(-bg)`, `priority-low(-bg)`, `tag-highlight(-bg)`) are unaffected by name but change TIER: each now points at a semantic token (`{semantic.color.X}`) instead of a primitive, so scripts/tokens-lib.mjs's cssValueForRef emits a single `var(--color-<semantic-name>)` line for them (dark mode cascades through the semantic token's own override, no separate dark line needed for the alias) — see design/figma-map.json's naming table / issue #203 for the full old->new list and the rename script's own record of the diff proof. TICKET #204 (2026-08-11): resolved the 13 $pendingFigmaValue deviations #203 flagged (all dark-mode, plus surface-highlight-red-hover/-active's light values) by cross-checking each against BOTH the live node fetch (get_variable_defs on the fetched Button/Input-field state nodes) and design/figma-variables/Semantics _ Style_Dark.tokens.json directly — every one landed exactly on the value #203 had already provisionally recorded, so this ticket applied them as-is (no further guessing). Also fixed the real bug #203's rename inherited unexamined: Figma's ramps run default->selected->hover->active, but Button/White and Button/Distructive's CSS states were bound one column off (Hover reading the `selected` variable, Active reading the `hover` variable, Selected reading nothing/`default`) — confirmed per-state, per-variant by fetching each of the 8 individual state nodes (not assumed from the ticket's own hypothesis), see design/notes/Button.md's #204 entry for the full node-by-node table. Two new tokens back the corrected ramp: `surface-highlight-white-hover` (stone-200) and `surface-highlight-white-active` (stone-300) — White's Hover/Active previously borrowed `surface-highlight-white-selected`/`surface-secondary` pixel-for-pixel (byte-identical in light mode, which is exactly why the bug was invisible); Transparent's Hover/Active, measured independently on its own fetched nodes rather than assumed from matching pixels, turned out to read these SAME white-ramp variables (not `surface-secondary`/`surface-secondary-hover`, which happen to share only the light-mode hex) — its dark-mode pixels do change as a result (verified: `surface-secondary-hover` dark stone-700 vs `surface-highlight-white-hover` dark stone-500), so this is a real rebind, not a naming no-op. `surface-highlight-white-selected` and `surface-highlight-red-selected` (the latter new, red-100) now back real Selected fills for the first time — Selected touches `background-color`, the same property Hover/Active already use on these styles, so `buttonVariants`' white/destructive entries gain the same `aria-pressed:hover:`/`aria-pressed:active:` compound-variant pattern #68 established for Outline's border (verified against the compiled `pnpm ladle:build` stylesheet, not assumed — see design/notes/Button.md). `priority-urgent-bg-selected` added as the matching alias-tier entry for Destructive's new Selected fill. `surface-hover` (stone-50, #203's flagged orphan) is deleted: CardDetailPanel.tsx's two option-row hovers had no Figma node of their own, so per the ticket's fallback rule they now read the ramp of their surrounding surface (the Dropdown panel's own `bg-surface-highlight-white`) — i.e. `surface-highlight-white-hover`, the same new token Button/White's Hover uses; design/notes/CardDetailPanel.md records the reasoning. Two deliberately-accepted-not-fixed dark-mode quirks, both confirmed as genuine Figma facts (not codebase artifacts) via the Style_Dark export: `surface-highlight-red(-hover/-active/-selected)` are all identical to `surface-highlight-red`'s own light value in dark mode (red-50), so Destructive's hover/active/selected fills are indistinguishable from Default there; and `surface-highlight-white-active`'s dark value (stone-400) is lighter than `-hover`'s (stone-500), backwards from the light-mode escalation direction. `button-vs-input-active-border` (docs/open-questions.md) is closed: fetched Button/Outline's Active node (bound to `Stroke/secondary/active`, stone-800) and Input-field's Active node (bound to `Stroke/primary/active`, stone-600) side by side — two different, correctly-bound Figma variables, not one ramp read inconsistently. `surface-primary` and `stroke-lines` get real dark values for the first time (stone-900, stone-400) — `surface-primary` backs `<body>` (app/layout.tsx), so this is also a real bug fix: the page background previously had no dark override at all and stayed light-mode-coloured under `[data-theme="dark"]`.

surface-highlight-white-hover.$comment: NEW (#204): Button/White's Hover fill genuinely reads this variable (color/surface/highlight/white/hover), confirmed on the fetched Hover-state node — not the same variable as White's Selected, which the pre-#204 code had it borrowing due to the default->selected->hover->active column-shift bug. Also backs Transparent's Hover (measured on its own fetched node, not assumed from matching pixels) and CardDetailPanel.tsx's Prioriteit/Grootte option-row hover (no Figma node of its own for that row; borrows the surrounding Dropdown panel's own surface-highlight-white family, see design/notes/CardDetailPanel.md).

surface-highlight-white-active.$comment: NEW (#204): Button/White's Active fill, and (measured on its own fetched node) Transparent's Active. Dark value (stone-400) is LIGHTER than -hover's dark value (stone-500) — backwards from the light-mode escalation direction, same shape as the pre-#204 known gap this supersedes. Sourced directly from Figma's Style_Dark export, not derived here — flagged, not fixed, per the ticket's 'Figma wins even where it hurts' instruction.

surface-highlight-red-selected.$comment: NEW (#204): Destructive's Selected fill, previously unmodelled (Selected read as bg-unchanged/'identical to Default', which was actually the pre-#204 column-shift bug's Default->Selected slot, not a deliberate no-fill state — the fetched Selected-state node's own bound variable is this one, red/selected, not red/default). Destructive's Selected TEXT still does not change (no text variable on that node, matching the existing 'Distructive text never changes' rule) — only the fill is new.

priority-urgent-bg-selected.$comment: NEW (#204), same alias tier as priority-urgent-bg(-hover/-active): backs Atom/Button's destructive Selected fill.

duration.$comment: Ticket #86 (Sidebar collapse slide): the motion token layer this repo was missing. No Figma prototype spec exists to sync (see the primitive.duration $comment) — `base` is this codebase's own default, not a Figma-sourced value, flagged at docs/open-questions.md#sidebar-motion-timing-unsourced pending a design/product answer. `pnpm sync:tokens` emits it as `--duration-base` in app/theme.css's @theme block. IMPORTANT: unlike `--ease-*`, `--duration-*` is NOT a Tailwind v4 theme namespace — there is no generated `duration-base` utility, and writing one compiles to nothing and silently falls back to `--default-transition-duration` (150ms). Consumers must reference it as an arbitrary value: `duration-[var(--duration-base)]`. No dark-mode split applies to motion.

easing.$comment: Ticket #86, same rationale as semantic.duration above. `base` reuses the standard ease-out curve (see primitive.easing.$comment) under a project-owned name so a future retune has exactly one place to change, instead of the raw `ease-out` Tailwind utility Dropdown.tsx/ButtonToggle.tsx each already reach for directly today (their own doc comments flag this same gap — not migrated by this ticket, out of scope for a Sidebar-only fix, but a natural follow-up once this token exists).

typography.$comment: Figma text styles are Tailwind-native; no CSS generation needed. This is the authoritative mapping for agents (font: Inter).
